entry.author: Whaikaha — Ministry of Disabled People
entry.summary:
Whaikaha is pleased to open consultation on New Zealand’s draft disability strategy. In this video, Whaikaha CEO Paula Tesoriero shares the news alongside an NZSL interpeter.

Consultation closes on Sunday 28 September. Please make sure you have your say. 

The draft strategy is important because it will guide the Government’s work for the next 5 years, and it's now time to hear what you think of it. 

To find out more and give your thoughts, visit www.whaikaha.govt.nz/disability-strategy

Full script:

Tēnā koutou katoa, Talofa Lava, Mālō a leilei, Bula vinaka, warm Pacific greetings.     

My name is Paula, I’m the chief executive of the Ministry of Disabled People - Whaikaha.  

My sign name is this (demonstrates move) which is two fists moving in a forward direction like a bicycle. 

Today, Whaikaha is pleased to be opening consultation on New Zealand’s draft disability strategy. 

Our current disability strategy will end next year.  The draft strategy is important because it will guide the Government’s work for the next five years and it's now time to hear what you think of it.
 
We’ve worked with members of the disability community – as well as Government and sector representatives – to create the draft.  We are grateful for the time and expertise people have provided, alongside a willingness to collaborate.  

The draft strategy includes a new vision and new principles. There are also goals and actions in areas that are important to disabled people such as employment, health, housing, education and justice.  

There’re lots of ways to provide feedback such as filling out our online feedback form, or by registering to attend an online or in-person meeting. 

You can details and copies of the strategy, in alternate formats, on our website at www.whaikaha.govt.nz/disability-strategy 

Consultation closes on Sunday 28 September. Make sure you have your say. 

Let’s make New Zealand a place where disabled people thrive.
